idiom_name: function* typed Generator<T, TReturn, TNext> / IterableIterator<T>
implementation_notes: TypeScript types the JavaScript generator protocol rather than adding one: a generator function infers Generator<T, TReturn, TNext> (or IterableIterator<T> when only the iteration surface is exposed), Iterable<T>/Iterator<T> describe what consumers require, and the compiler checks the value passed to next() against TNext. Set target (or lib) to ES2015 or later, or enable downlevelIteration, so for...of, spread and yield* compile to protocol calls instead of index loops; the async form needs an ES2018 target and TypeScript 2.3 or later, which added async iterators and generators.
pitfalls: The inferred third parameter defaults to unknown/void when a generator's type parameters never appear in it; annotate Generator<T, TReturn, TNext> explicitly when callers send values back with next(v), or the compiler rejects the call.

for...of over a non-array iterable compiles to iterator protocol calls only with target ES2015+ or downlevelIteration; without it TypeScript emits an index loop that silently iterates a Set/Map/generator zero times.

Iterable<T> is structural, so a single-use generator object is assignable where a re-iterable collection is expected; model the difference in the API (IterableIterator<T> versus Iterable<T>) rather than letting callers discover it on the second pass.

variants.name: Typed async generators (AsyncGenerator<T>, for await...of)
variants.idiom_name: async function* AsyncGenerator<T> consumed by for await...of
variants.implementation_notes: The async generator form is typed as AsyncGenerator<T, TReturn, TNext> (or AsyncIterableIterator<T>), consumed with for await...of and driven by the same protocol shape where next() resolves to IteratorResult. It requires TypeScript 2.3 or later plus an ES2018 runtime target (downlevel emit of async iteration is limited), and it is what streaming APIs type themselves against; keep the synchronous generator when nothing is awaited, because the async state machine costs an allocation and a promise per element.
pitfalls: Typing the loop variable by hand loses the generator's element type when the source is a union of async iterables; declare the generator's return type so AsyncGenerator<T> drives inference instead of unknown.

Async generators and cancellation: breaking out of for await...of only signals return(), so the fetch stream stays open unless the generator's finally block (or an AbortController tied to the loop) closes it.
